input: File a claim for the damaged luggage from my flight

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The extent and type of damage determines whether this is an airline claim, travel insurance claim, or both — and affects what compensation is realistically available.
Whether the user is filing alone or needs help from a travel agent, insurance broker, or airline rep changes what steps they need to take themselves.
The airline and whether the flight was domestic or international (governed by different conventions, e.g. Montreal Convention) fundamentally changes the claims process and liability limits.
Airlines and insurers have strict deadlines — often 7 days for damage claims — so knowing how much time has passed since the flight is critical to the plan.
Whether the user has already reported the damage at the airport (Property Irregularity Report) determines whether there is a reference number to build the claim on or if that step is still needed.
The user's goal — full reimbursement, repair cost, or a replacement — shapes what evidence to gather and how assertively to pursue the claim.
Whether the user prefers to file online, by phone, or in person, and whether they want step-by-step guidance or just a checklist, determines the format of the plan.

gold.taskTitle: File a damaged luggage claim for flight
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to submit a claim for luggage that was damaged during a flight, which involves identifying the right process, gathering documentation, and contacting the right parties.

questions.title: Which airline operated the flight with the damaged bag?
questions.description: Identifying the airline determines exactly where and how to file, what their specific claims portal or process is, and what liability limits apply.

questions.title: Was this a domestic or international flight?
questions.description: Domestic vs. international flights are governed by different legal frameworks (e.g. Montreal Convention for international), which changes compensation limits and filing rules.

questions.title: How many days ago did the flight land?
questions.description: Most airlines require damage to be reported within 7 days; knowing the timeline determines urgency and whether the standard deadline has passed.

questions.title: Did you file a Property Irregularity Report at the airport?
questions.description: A PIR filed at the airport is often a prerequisite for a formal claim; knowing whether one exists determines the starting point of the plan.

questions.title: Are you claiming through the airline, travel insurance, or both?
questions.description: The claiming route changes the documentation required, the process to follow, and the realistic compensation outcome.

questions.title: What outcome are you hoping to get from this claim?
questions.description: Whether the user wants full replacement value, repair reimbursement, or a travel voucher shapes how to frame the claim and what evidence to prioritise.

questions.title: Do you prefer to handle this online, by phone, or in person?
questions.description: The user's preferred channel determines whether the plan focuses on the airline's web portal, a customer service call script, or visiting an airport desk.
